events_run1: A governor cleared everyone else from the room.
He wept aloud and revealed himself to his brothers.
He asked whether his father was still alive, and his brothers were too troubled to answer.
He told them to come near, and they did.
He told them that God had sent him ahead to save lives during the famine.
He sent them to bring their father to live near him.
He embraced his youngest brother and wept, then kissed all his brothers.
The king heard the news and was pleased.
The king told the brothers to take wagons and bring their father and families to the land.
The governor gave them wagons, provisions, clothing, silver, and gifts for their father.
The brothers returned to their homeland and told their father the governor was alive.
The father did not believe them at first, but when he saw the wagons his spirit revived, and he resolved to go see his son.
events_run2: A ruler cries out for everyone else to leave the room.
The ruler reveals himself to his brothers and weeps so loudly that the household hears.
The brothers are too frightened to answer him.
The ruler tells them to come near and says they sold him into slavery.
He sends them to bring their father to live near him during the famine.
The ruler embraces his youngest brother and kisses and weeps over all his brothers.
The king hears of it and is pleased, and he tells the brothers to fetch their father and families.
The brothers are given wagons, provisions, and clothing, with extra gifts for the youngest.
The ruler sends gifts of animals loaded with food for his father.
The brothers return to their homeland and tell their father his son is alive.
The father faints, not believing them, until he sees the wagons.
The father revives and resolves to go see his son before he dies.

events_run1: A king finished building the temple and his own palace.
God appeared to the king a second time.
God promised to keep the king's throne if he stayed faithful, and warned of ruin if he turned to other gods.
After twenty years, the king gave a neighboring king twenty cities.
The neighboring king came to see the cities and was displeased with them.
The neighboring king sent the king a large amount of gold.
The king raised a levy of labor to build the temple, his palace, and the city walls and other cities.
A foreign ruler had earlier captured a city, burned it, and given it to his daughter, the king's wife.
The king rebuilt that city and many others, including storage and chariot cities.
The king put the surviving native peoples to forced labor.
The foreign ruler's daughter moved into the house the king built for her.
The king built a fleet at a seaport, and the neighboring king's sailors sailed it to a distant land and brought back gold.
events_run2: A king finished building the temple and his own palace.
God appeared to the king a second time.
God promised to keep the king's throne if he stayed faithful, and warned of ruin if he turned to other gods.
After twenty years, the king gave twenty cities to a neighboring king who had supplied him with building materials.
The neighboring king came to see the cities and was displeased with them.
The neighboring king sent the king a large amount of gold.
The king raised a labor levy and built cities, walls and storehouses across his land.
A foreign ruler had earlier captured and burned a city, then given it to his daughter, the king's wife.
The king made the surviving foreign peoples into forced laborers.
The king's wife moved from the old city to the house he built for her.
Three times a year the king offered sacrifices and incense at the altar.
The king built a fleet at a seaport, and the neighboring king's sailors sailed with it to a distant land and brought back gold.

events_run1: A king began to reign and did evil, following the sins of an earlier king.
God's anger led to the people being handed over to a foreign king and his son.
The king prayed, and God gave the people a saviour who freed them from the foreign oppressors.
The foreign king's wars left the army almost destroyed.
The king died and was buried in the capital, and his son became king.
The new king also did evil and fought against the king of a neighboring kingdom.
The new king died and was buried in the capital.
The prophet fell sick, and the king came and wept over him.
At the prophet's command, the king shot an arrow from an open window, then struck the ground with arrows only three times.
The prophet was angry that he stopped and said the king would defeat the enemy only three times.
The prophet died and was buried, and raiders invaded the land.
A dead man thrown into the prophet's tomb touched his bones and came back to life.
events_run2: A new king began to rule over his people and did evil.
The people's God grew angry and gave them into the power of a foreign king and his son.
The king begged his God for help.
God heard him and sent a saviour, and the people got free of their oppressors.
The foreign king had left the king only a small army.
The king died and was buried in the capital, and his son became king.
The new king also did evil, fought against the king of a neighbouring land, then died and was buried.
A prophet fell sick, and the king came and wept over him.
The prophet had the king take a bow and arrows, open a window, and shoot an arrow toward the enemy.
The prophet told the king to strike the ground with the arrows, and he struck three times and stopped.
The prophet was angry and said the king would defeat the enemy only three times.
The prophet died and was buried, and raiders invaded the land.

events_run1: The king gave a villain's house to the queen.
The queen's cousin came before the king and received the king's ring.
The queen put her cousin in charge of the villain's house.
The queen fell at the king's feet in tears and begged him to undo the villain's plot against her people.
The king held out his golden sceptre to her.
She asked that letters be written to reverse the villain's orders to destroy her people.
The king told them to write on behalf of the Jews and seal it with his ring.
The king's scribes were called and wrote out the decree as the queen's cousin commanded.
Riders on horses, mules and camels carried the letters to every province.
The decree let the Jews in every city gather and defend themselves against any who attacked them on one appointed day.
The queen's cousin left the king in royal robes and a golden crown, and the city rejoiced.
The Jews held feasts and celebrated, and many people of the land became Jews out of fear.
events_run2: The king gave a murdered enemy's house to the queen.
The queen's cousin came before the king, and the king gave him his ring.
The queen set her cousin over the enemy's house.
The queen fell at the king's feet, weeping, and begged him to undo the enemy's plot against her people.
The king held out the golden sceptre to her, and she stood and asked that the letters be reversed.
The king told them to write for the Jews in his name and seal it with his ring.
The scribes were called and wrote out the decree as the queen's cousin commanded.
Riders on horses, mules and camels carried the letters to every province.
The decree let the Jews gather and defend themselves against their enemies on one appointed day.
The queen's cousin left the king in royal robes and a golden crown.
The city rejoiced.
The Jews held feasts across the provinces, and many people of the land became Jews out of fear.

events_run1: A man from one tribe took forbidden spoils from a conquered city.
A leader sent men to scout the next city.
The scouts returned and advised sending only a few thousand men.
About three thousand men went up and fled before the city's defenders.
The defenders killed about thirty-six of them and chased them from the gate.
The leader tore his clothes and lay on his face before the ark until evening, with the elders.
God told the leader to rise and said the people had sinned by taking forbidden spoils.
The leader rose early and brought the people forward by tribe, family and household until the guilty man was picked.
The guilty man confessed that he had coveted and taken a garment, silver and gold, and hidden them in his tent.
Messengers ran to the tent and found the goods hidden there.
The people took the man, his family, his animals and his goods to a valley.
The people stoned and burned them and raised a heap of stones over them.
events_run2: A man of one tribe took forbidden spoils for himself.
The leader sent men to scout the next city.
The scouts reported that the city was weak and only a few thousand men were needed.
About three thousand men went up and were driven off in flight.
The city's men killed about thirty-six of them and chased them down the slope.
The leader tore his clothes and lay on his face before the ark until evening, with the elders.
God told him that the people had sinned by taking the forbidden things and must be cleansed.
The leader brought the people forward by tribe, family, household and man, and the thief was chosen.
The thief confessed that he had coveted a garment, silver and gold from the spoils and hidden them in his tent.
Messengers ran to the tent and found the goods hidden there.
The people brought the thief, his family, his animals, his goods and the stolen items to a valley.
The people stoned and burned them, raised a heap of stones over them, and named the place.

events_run1: A king speaks his final words about how a just ruler should rule.
A great warrior lifts his spear against eight hundred men and kills them at one time.
A second warrior fights a gathered enemy army until his hand is weary and clings to his sword, and the people win a great victory.
A third warrior stands in a field of lentils, defends it, and kills the enemy as the people flee.
Three of the king's chief men come to him at a cave in harvest time while the enemy camps in a valley.
The king longs for a drink from the well of his hometown, which the enemy garrison holds.
The three mighty men break through the enemy army, draw water from the well, and bring it to the king.
The king refuses to drink the water and pours it out as an offering.
A commander's brother lifts his spear against three hundred men and kills them.
Another warrior kills two enemy men, and kills a lion in a pit on a snowy day.
He takes a spear from a giant foreign man with only a staff and kills him with it.
The king sets him over his guard.
events_run2: A king speaks his last words about how a just ruler should rule.
A mighty warrior raises his spear against eight hundred men and kills them at one time.
A second warrior fights the enemy until his hand is weary and clings to his sword, and a great victory follows.
A third warrior stands in a field of lentils, defends it alone against the enemy, and kills them while the people flee.
Three warriors come to the king at a cave during harvest time while the enemy camps in a valley.
The king, hiding in a stronghold while the enemy holds his hometown, longs for water from the town's well.
The three warriors break through the enemy army, draw water from the well, and bring it to the king.
The king refuses to drink the water and pours it out as an offering.
Another warrior raises his spear against three hundred men and kills them.
A warrior kills two fierce men, then kills a lion in a pit on a snowy day.
The same warrior takes a spear from a large enemy man with only a staff and kills him with it.
The king sets that warrior over his guard.

events_run1: A young man is taken to a foreign land and sold to an officer of the ruler.
The officer sees that the young man prospers, so he puts him in charge of his whole house.
The officer's household is blessed because of the young man.
The officer's wife asks the young man to lie with her.
He refuses, and she keeps asking him day after day.
One day, when no one else is in the house, she grabs his garment.
He leaves the garment in her hand and flees outside.
She calls the household servants and falsely says he tried to attack her.
She keeps the garment until her husband comes home, then tells him the same false story.
The angry officer puts the young man in the prison where the king's prisoners are held.
The keeper of the prison favors the young man and puts all the prisoners in his care.
events_run2: A young man is taken to a foreign land and sold to an officer of the ruler.
The officer sees that the young man prospers in everything he does.
The officer makes him overseer of the whole household.
The household is blessed because of him.
The officer's wife asks him to lie with her, and he refuses.
She keeps asking day after day, and he keeps refusing.
One day, alone in the house with her, he is caught by his garment, leaves it in her hand, and flees.
She calls the household men and falsely accuses him of attacking her.
She keeps the garment until her husband returns, then tells him the same lie.
The husband grows angry and puts the young man in the prison where the king's prisoners are held.
The prison keeper favors him and puts all the prisoners in his charge.
Everything he does in the prison prospers.

events_run1: A new governor arrived in the province and, three days later, went up to the capital city.
The chief priest and Jewish leaders accused a prisoner to him and asked him to send the prisoner to the city, planning an ambush to kill him on the way.
The governor refused and said the prisoner would stay in the coastal city, where he himself would soon go.
The governor stayed in the capital more than ten days and then returned to the coastal city.
The next day he sat on the judgment seat and ordered the prisoner brought in.
The accusers from the capital stood around and made many serious charges they could not prove.
The prisoner denied any offense and, when asked whether he would be tried in the capital, appealed to the emperor.
The governor conferred with his council and granted the appeal.
After some days a king and his sister-wife arrived at the coastal city to greet the governor.
The governor told the king about the prisoner left by his predecessor and about the accusers' charges.
The king asked to hear the prisoner himself.
The next day the king arrived with great pomp, and the governor had the prisoner brought before the assembly.
events_run2: A new governor arrives in the province and goes up to the capital city after three days.
The chief priest and leaders ask him to send the prisoner to the city, planning an ambush to kill him on the way.
The governor refuses and says the prisoner will stay in the coastal city, where he will soon return.
After staying more than ten days, the governor goes back down to the coastal city.
The next day he sits on the judgment seat and orders the prisoner brought in.
The accusers from the capital stand around and bring serious charges they cannot prove.
The prisoner denies any offense, and the governor asks if he will be tried in the capital.
The prisoner refuses and appeals to the emperor.
The governor confers with his council and grants the appeal.
Some days later a king and his wife come to the coastal city to greet the governor.
The governor tells the king about the prisoner, and the king asks to hear him.
The next day the king and his wife enter the hall with great pomp, and the prisoner is brought out.

events_run1: An old master tells his chief servant to swear an oath not to take a wife for his son from the local people.
The servant swears the oath.
The servant takes ten camels and travels to a distant city.
He makes the camels kneel by a well in the evening and prays for a sign.
A young woman comes to the well and gives him and his camels water.
The servant gives her gold jewelry and asks to lodge at her father's house.
The servant worships, and the young woman runs to tell her family.
Her brother runs to the well and brings the servant into the house.
The servant refuses to eat until he has told his errand, then tells the whole story.
The woman's family agrees she should go, and the servant gives gifts and worships.
The next morning the family asks her to stay, but she agrees to leave at once.
She travels home with the servant and meets the son, who takes her as his wife.
events_run2: An old master tells his chief servant to swear an oath not to take a wife for the master's son from the local people.
The servant swears the oath, promising to find a wife among the master's own kin.
The servant takes ten camels and travels to the city of the master's kindred.
He makes the camels kneel by a well in the evening and prays for a sign.
A young woman comes to the well, gives him a drink, and offers to water his camels too.
The servant gives her a gold earring and two bracelets and asks to lodge at her father's house.
She says she is of the master's kin and that there is room, and the servant worships.
Her brother runs to the well and brings the servant and his camels into the house.
The servant refuses to eat until he tells his errand, then tells the whole story.
The woman's father and brother agree she should go, and the servant gives gifts to her and her family.
The next morning the servant asks to leave, and the woman agrees to go, so her family blesses her and sends her off.
She travels with the servant, sees the master's son in a field, covers herself with a veil, and becomes his wife.

events_run1: A dying king tells his son to be strong and keep the law.
The king tells his son to punish a general who killed two captains in peacetime.
The king asks his son to show kindness to the sons of a man who helped him when he fled.
The king tells his son to put to death a man who cursed him.
The old king dies and is buried in the city.
The son takes the throne and his kingdom is established.
The new king's older brother asks the king's mother to request a wife for him.
The mother asks the king to give his brother the woman, and the king angrily has the brother put to death.
The king banishes a priest to his own fields for supporting the brother.
The general flees to the tabernacle and holds the altar, refusing to leave, so the king's officer kills him there.
The king appoints new men over the army and the priesthood.
The king confines the cursing man to the city, and when he leaves to fetch runaway servants, the king has him killed.
events_run2: A dying king charges his son to keep the law and to deal with two men who wronged him.
The old king dies and is buried in the city.
The son sits on the throne and his kingdom is established.
The king's elder brother asks the king's mother to request a wife for him.
The mother goes to the king, who honors her with a seat at his right hand.
She makes the request, and the king refuses it and accuses his brother of seeking the kingdom.
The king swears an oath and sends a man who kills his brother.
The king banishes a priest to his own fields and removes him from the priesthood.
The commander flees to the tabernacle and holds the altar's horns, refusing to come out.
The king orders the commander killed at the altar, and the man he sent kills him.
The king appoints a new commander and a new priest.
The king confines a man who cursed his father to the city, and the man later leaves to retrieve runaway servants, so the king has him killed.

events_run1: A king defeated a neighboring people and took one of their towns.
He conquered another nation, killed many of its people, and made the survivors his servants who paid tribute.
He defeated a rival king who was going to restore his border at the great river.
He captured the rival king's chariots, horsemen and foot soldiers, and crippled most of the chariot horses.
A foreign army came to help the rival king, and the king killed twenty-two thousand of them.
He set garrisons in the foreign capital, and its people became his servants.
He took the gold shields and a great deal of brass from the rival king's cities and brought them to the capital.
Another king heard of the victory and sent his son to greet and bless the conquering king.
The son brought gifts of silver, gold and brass, which the king dedicated to God along with the spoil from all the nations he had conquered.
The king won fame by defeating eighteen thousand enemies in a valley on his return.
He placed garrisons throughout the neighboring land of Edom, and its people became his servants.
He reigned over all his people and appointed officers, priests and a scribe.
events_run2: A king defeated an enemy people and took a city from them.
The king conquered a neighboring nation and measured its people with lines to decide who died and who lived.
The conquered nation became his servants and brought him gifts.
The king defeated a rival king who was going to restore his border at a great river.
He captured a thousand chariots, seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and crippled most of the chariot horses.
A neighboring people came to help the rival king, and the king killed twenty-two thousand of them.
He placed garrisons in their land, and they became his servants and brought gifts.
He took the golden shields and a great amount of brass from the rival king's cities and brought them to the capital.
A distant king, hearing of the victory, sent his son with silver, gold and brass vessels to greet and bless him.
The king dedicated those gifts, with the silver and gold from all the nations he had conquered, to God.
He won renown by defeating eighteen thousand men in a valley.
He placed garrisons throughout another nation, and its people became his servants.

events_run1: A king of a nation gathers his army, afraid, as an enemy army camps nearby.
An enemy army gathers for war against the nation.
A foreign ruler tells a warrior to join him in battle, and the warrior agrees.
The king asks God for guidance, but God gives no answer.
The king disguises himself and goes at night with two men to a woman who speaks with spirits.
The woman fears for her life, but the king swears she will not be punished.
At the king's request, the woman calls up a dead prophet.
The woman sees the figure rise, realizes her visitor is the king, and cries out.
The dead prophet tells the king that he and his sons will die and the nation will fall to the enemy.
The king collapses to the ground in fear, weak from not having eaten.
The woman and the king's servants persuade the reluctant king to eat.
The woman bakes bread and a calf, and the king and his servants eat and leave that night.
events_run2: A king of a people prepared for war against his enemies, and a foreign king told a fugitive he must fight alongside him.
The fugitive agreed, and the foreign king promised to make him his bodyguard.
The enemy armies camped in one place, and the king gathered his own people to camp on a mountain.
The king saw the enemy host and was terrified.
The king asked God for guidance, but God did not answer him.
The king disguised himself and went by night with two men to a woman who spoke with spirits.
The woman feared a trap, but the king swore she would not be punished.
At his request, the woman called up a dead prophet.
The woman cried out when she saw the prophet and recognized the king.
The prophet told the king that God had left him, the kingdom would pass to another, and he and his sons would die in battle the next day.
The king fell to the ground in fear, and the woman and his servants persuaded him to eat.
The woman killed a calf and baked bread, and the king and his servants ate and left that night.

events_run1: A king of a distant empire attacked, and a local king served him for three years.
The local king then rebelled against the empire's king.
Raiding bands from neighboring peoples were sent against the kingdom to destroy it.
The local king died, and his son became king.
The son, a young man, ruled in the city for three months and did evil.
The empire's servants came up against the city and besieged it.
The empire's king came to the city himself.
The young king surrendered to the empire's king with his mother, servants, princes and officers.
The empire's king took the temple and palace treasures and cut up the gold vessels.
He carried off the young king, the leaders, the warriors and the craftsmen as captives, leaving only the poorest people.
The empire's king made the young king's uncle king in his place and renamed him.
The new king ruled in the city and did evil, then rebelled against the empire's king.
events_run2: A king of a great empire attacked his neighbor's land, and its ruler served him for three years before rebelling.
God sent raiding bands from several nearby peoples against the rebel kingdom to destroy it.
The rebel ruler died, and his son became king.
The empire's king took all the land that had belonged to the king of Egypt, so Egypt's king stopped coming out of his land.
The young new king reigned three months and did evil.
The empire's servants attacked the city and besieged it.
The empire's king came to the city, and the young king went out to him with his mother, servants, princes and officers.
The empire's king took him captive and carried off the treasures of the temple and the palace, cutting up the gold vessels.
He carried away the city's princes, warriors, craftsmen and smiths, leaving only the poorest people behind.
He took the young king, his mother, wives and officers to the empire's capital in captivity.
He made the young king's uncle king in his place and changed his name.
The new king reigned eleven years and did evil, then rebelled against the empire's king.

events_run1: A king began to reign over a kingdom and did evil.
The king of a great empire attacked him, and he became that king's servant and paid tribute.
The king sent messengers to another king, in a neighboring land, and stopped paying tribute.
The great king found out about the plot, shut him up and bound him in prison.
The great king invaded the whole land and besieged the capital for three years.
The great king took the city and carried the people away to distant lands.
The great king brought settlers from other lands and placed them in the emptied cities.
The settlers did not honor the local God, so lions were sent among them and killed some.
The settlers told the great king about the lions.
The great king ordered that one of the exiled priests be sent back to teach them.
A priest returned, settled in a town, and taught them how to honor God.
Each settler nation also made its own gods and worshipped them alongside God.
events_run2: A king began to reign over a kingdom and did evil.
The king of a great empire attacked him, and he became that king's servant and paid him tribute.
He sent messengers to another king for help and stopped paying tribute.
The great king found the plot, shut him up, and bound him in prison.
The great king invaded the whole land and besieged the capital city for three years.
The great king captured the city and carried the people away to distant lands.
The great king brought settlers from other lands and placed them in the emptied cities.
The settlers did not honor the God of the land, so lions were sent among them and killed some.
The settlers told the great king about the lions.
The great king commanded that one of the exiled priests be sent back to teach them.
A priest came back, lived in a town, and taught them how to honor God.
Each settler nation made its own gods and kept worshipping them alongside God.

events_run1: A famine continued in the land, and a family ran out of the grain they had brought from a foreign country.
The father told his sons to go back and buy more food.
One son reminded him that the ruler had refused to see them unless their youngest brother came along.
The father reluctantly agreed to send the youngest son, after that son promised to take responsibility for him.
The father told them to take gifts, double money, and the money returned in their sacks.
The brothers traveled to the foreign country with the gifts, the money, and their youngest brother, and stood before the ruler.
The ruler saw the youngest brother and ordered his steward to bring the men to his house for a meal.
The frightened brothers told the steward about the money found in their sacks and offered to pay it back.
The steward reassured them and brought out their imprisoned brother to them.
The steward gave them water to wash their feet and fed their animals.
The brothers bowed to the ruler when he came home, and he asked about their father.
The ruler saw his youngest brother, wept privately, then returned and served the meal, giving the youngest brother five times as much.
events_run2: A famine continued, and a family ran out of the grain they had brought from a foreign land.
The father told his sons to go back and buy more food.
One son reminded him that the ruler there would not see them unless their youngest brother came along.
The father reluctantly agreed to send the youngest brother, and told them to bring gifts and double money.
The brothers took the gifts, the money, and the youngest brother, and travelled to the foreign land.
The ruler saw the youngest brother and ordered his steward to bring the men to his house for a noon meal.
The frightened brothers told the steward about the money found in their sacks and offered to repay it.
The steward reassured them and brought out the brother who had been held captive.
The steward gave them water to wash their feet and fed their animals.
When the ruler came home, the brothers gave him the gifts and bowed to the ground.
The ruler asked about their father, saw his youngest brother, and left the room to weep in private.
The ruler washed his face, returned, and had the meal served, giving the youngest brother five times as much food as the others.

events_run1: A god creates the heaven and the earth out of a formless, dark void.
The god makes light and separates it from the darkness, naming them day and night.
The god makes a dome in the sky to divide the waters above from the waters below.
The god gathers the waters into seas so dry land appears.
The earth brings forth grass, plants and fruit trees.
The god makes the sun, the moon and the stars to light the earth and mark time.
The god fills the waters with sea creatures and the sky with birds, and blesses them.
The god makes the cattle, the beasts and the creeping things of the land.
The god creates man and woman in his own image.
The god blesses them and gives them rule over all living things.
The god gives plants to people and animals for food.
The god sees all he has made and calls it very good.
events_run2: A god creates the heavens and the earth.
The god makes light and separates it from the darkness, calling them day and night.
The god makes a dome in the sky to divide the waters above from the waters below.
The god gathers the waters into seas so dry land appears.
The earth grows grass, plants and fruit trees.
The god makes the sun, the moon and the stars to light the earth and mark time.
The god fills the waters with sea creatures and the sky with birds, and blesses them.
The god makes the land animals, cattle and creeping things.
The god creates man and woman in his own image.
The god blesses them and gives them rule over all living things.
The god gives plants as food to people and animals.
The god sees all that he has made and calls it very good.

events_run1: Missionaries passed through two cities and arrived at a city with a synagogue.
A missionary reasoned with the Jews there from the scriptures for three sabbath days.
Some Jews, many devout Greeks, and several prominent women believed.
The unbelieving Jews gathered a mob of bad men and set the city in an uproar.
The mob attacked a believer's house and dragged him and some others before the city rulers.
The rulers took security from the believers and let them go.
The believers sent the missionaries away by night to another city.
The Jews from the first city followed them there and stirred up the crowd.
The believers sent the missionary on toward the sea and then to a great city.
In the great city he argued daily with Jews and in the market, and philosophers challenged him.
They brought him to a hill and asked him to explain his new teaching.
He spoke to them there, and some mocked, some wanted to hear more, and a few believed.
events_run2: A group of travelers passed through two towns and arrived at a city with a synagogue.
A teacher went into the synagogue and reasoned from the scriptures with the people for three sabbath days.
Some of the Jews, many devout Greeks, and several leading women believed.
The unbelieving Jews, moved by envy, gathered a mob of rough men and set the city in an uproar.
The mob attacked a host's house looking for the teachers.
Not finding them, the mob dragged the host and some believers before the city rulers and accused them.
The rulers took security from the host and the others and let them go.
The believers sent the teachers away by night to another town, where they preached in the synagogue and many believed.
The unbelieving Jews from the first city came to the second town and stirred up the crowds.
The believers sent the teacher on toward the sea, and an escort brought him to a great city.
In the great city, the teacher argued daily in the synagogue and market, and philosophers brought him to a hill to explain his teaching.
Most listeners mocked or put him off after he spoke, but a few men and a woman joined him.

events_run1: The tribes' leaders distributed the land of Canaan by lot among the nine and a half tribes.
A tribe's people came to the leader at the camp.
An old warrior reminded the leader of a promise made to him by the prophet.
He recalled being sent at forty years old to scout the land.
He said his companions had frightened the people, but he had followed God fully.
He said the prophet had promised him the land he had walked on.
He said he had been kept alive forty-five years since, and was now eighty-five and still strong.
He asked for the mountain, though giants and great walled cities were there.
The leader blessed him and gave him the city as his inheritance.
The city was named for a giant, a great man, who had lived there.
The land had rest from war.
events_run2: The leaders of the tribes distributed the land of inheritance to the nine and a half tribes by lot.
The people of one tribe came to their leader at the camp.
An elder of that tribe asked for what had been promised to him.
He recalled how, forty-five years earlier, the prophet had sent him to spy out the land.
He told how he brought back an honest report while the other spies made the people lose heart.
He recalled that the prophet had sworn to give him the land where he had walked.
He asked the leader for the hill country, saying he was still strong enough to drive out the giants in their walled cities.
The leader blessed him.
The leader gave him the city as an inheritance.
The city's old name was changed.
The land had rest from war.

events_run1: A mother-in-law tells a young widow to wash, dress, and go to the threshing floor at night.
The widow agrees and goes down to the floor.
She waits until a man has eaten and drunk and lain down at the end of the grain heap.
She quietly uncovers his feet and lies down.
At midnight the man wakes, startled, and finds a woman at his feet.
She tells him who she is and asks him to spread his cloak over her as a near kinsman.
He blesses her and promises to act as kinsman, noting that a nearer kinsman must be given the first chance.
She lies at his feet until early morning and leaves before anyone can recognize her.
He asks her to hold out her veil and fills it with six measures of barley.
She goes back into the city.
She tells her mother-in-law everything the man did.
The mother-in-law tells her to wait, since the man will settle the matter that day.
events_run2: A mother-in-law tells her daughter-in-law to wash, dress, and go to the threshing floor where a kinsman is winnowing barley.
The young woman goes to the floor and does as she was told.
After the man eats and drinks and lies down at the end of the grain heap, she quietly uncovers his feet and lies down.
At midnight the man wakes in fright and finds a woman at his feet.
She tells him who she is and asks him to spread his cloak over her as a near kinsman.
He blesses her, promises to do what she asks, and says a nearer kinsman must be given the first chance.
She lies at his feet until morning and rises before anyone can recognize her.
He tells her to keep the visit secret and has her hold out her veil.
He measures six measures of barley into the veil and puts it on her.
She goes back into the city.
She tells her mother-in-law everything the man did and shows the barley.
Her mother-in-law tells her to wait and see how the matter turns out.

events_run1: A deity appears to a man sitting at his tent door in the heat of the day.
The man sees three visitors, runs to meet them, and bows to the ground.
He invites them to rest and offers water and bread.
He hurries to his wife and asks her to bake cakes.
He fetches a tender calf, and a servant prepares it.
He serves the visitors the calf, butter and milk, and stands by while they eat.
The visitors promise that his elderly wife will have a son.
The wife overhears at the tent door and laughs to herself.
The deity asks why she laughed, and she denies it out of fear.
The visitors rise and look toward the wicked city, and the man walks with them.
The deity says he will go down to see whether the city's sin is as great as the cry against it.
The man pleads for the city, and the deity agrees to spare it for fifty, then fewer, down to ten righteous people.
events_run2: A prophet is visited by three men while sitting at his tent door in the heat of the day.
He runs to meet them and bows to the ground.
He offers them water, rest and bread, and they accept.
He hurries to have his wife bake cakes and has a calf prepared.
He sets the food before them and stands by them while they eat.
The visitors say his wife will have a son, and she overhears it from the tent door.
His wife laughs to herself, then denies it out of fear, and is told she did laugh.
The men rise and look toward the wicked city, and he walks with them to see them off.
The Lord says he will go down to see whether the city's sin is as great as the cry against it.
The men go toward the city while the prophet stays standing before the Lord.
The prophet pleads with the Lord to spare the city for fifty righteous people, then bargains down step by step to ten.
The Lord agrees each time, then leaves, and the prophet returns home.
